beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Scope and Faculty Flexibility as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. This course examines current topics in Systems. Consider this worked case: Instructors select specific course instances belonging to the Distributed Systems, Architecture and Operating Systems, or Security cluster. On screen, display a flowchart showing three selectable cluster paths (Distributed Systems, Architecture and Operating Systems, Security) converging into a central 'Seminar in Systems' node. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.

beats.narration: Now define Secure Software Development Framework Overview precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. The Secure Software Development Framework groups practices into four practice groups. Consider this worked case: Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development. On screen, show a four-quadrant diagram labeling each practice group with its core function. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Secure Software Development Framework Overview
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a four-quadrant diagram labeling each practice group with its core function.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Prepare the Organization Practice operates in a concrete sequence. Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development. Consider this worked case: Teams define security policies and allocate resources before writing code. On screen, illustrate a checklist with three items: 'Define security policies', 'Allocate resources', 'Establish development processes'. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis. Then summarize what the example demonstrates, what it does not establish, and what evidence would be needed next.
beats.title: Prepare the Organization Practice
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a checklist with three items: 'Define security policies', 'Allocate resources', 'Establish development processes'.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Protect the Software Practice and make the decision criteria explicit. Protect the Software prevents unauthorized access to code and development artifacts. Consider this worked case: Repositories use role-based access control to restrict who can view or modify source files. On screen, draw a locked vault icon with three access levels: 'Read', 'Write', 'Admin' labeled around it. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Protect the Software Practice
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Draw a locked vault icon with three access levels: 'Read', 'Write', 'Admin' labeled around it.

beats.narration: Apply Produce Well-Secured Software Practice to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Produce Well-Secured Software addresses security requirements, design, verification, and release. Consider this worked case: Developers verify that security requirements are met before deploying the final software version. On screen, create a pipeline graphic showing 'Requirements' -> 'Design' -> 'Verification' -> 'Release' with checkmarks at each stage. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Produce Well-Secured Software Practice
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Create a pipeline graphic showing 'Requirements' -> 'Design' -> 'Verification' -> 'Release' with checkmarks at each stage.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Respond to Vulnerabilities Practice, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Respond to Vulnerabilities identifies, analyzes, remediates, and learns from discovered weaknesses. Consider this worked case: When a bug is found, the team patches the code and updates the security documentation. On screen, show a circular diagram with arrows labeled 'Identify', 'Analyze', 'Remediate', 'Learn' connecting back to 'Identify'. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Respond to Vulnerabilities Practice
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a circular diagram with arrows labeled 'Identify', 'Analyze', 'Remediate', 'Learn' connecting back to 'Identify'.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Security Requirements and Reasoning with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Security reasoning identifies assets, trust boundaries, threats, controls, evidence, residual risk, and responsibilities. Consider this worked case: A system tracks user authentication requirements from design through testing. On screen, display a table with columns: 'Asset', 'Trust Boundary', 'Threat', 'Control', 'Evidence', 'Residual Risk', 'Responsibility'. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Security Requirements and Reasoning
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a table with columns: 'Asset', 'Trust Boundary', 'Threat', 'Control', 'Evidence', 'Residual Risk', 'Responsibility'.

beats.narration: Use Cryptographic Standards and Confidentiality to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Encryption supports confidentiality when keys and modes are used correctly. Consider this worked case: AES-256 encryption protects data in transit when paired with a secure key exchange protocol. On screen, show a padlock icon with a key inside, labeled 'AES-256', and a shield icon labeled 'Confidentiality'. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Cryptographic Standards and Confidentiality
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a padlock icon with a key inside, labeled 'AES-256', and a shield icon labeled 'Confidentiality'.

beats.narration: Connect Integrity, Authenticity, and Key Management to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Message authentication and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity in different ways. Consider this worked case: Digital signatures verify that a message was sent by a specific sender without alteration. On screen, draw two side-by-side icons: a stamp icon labeled 'Digital Signature' and a key ring icon labeled 'Key Management'. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Integrity, Authenticity, and Key Management
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Draw two side-by-side icons: a stamp icon labeled 'Digital Signature' and a key ring icon labeled 'Key Management'.

beats.narration: Finish with Modes of Operation and Side Channels as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Modes of operation define how a primitive processes data larger than one block. Consider this worked case: CBC mode processes data in blocks, but timing attacks can expose vulnerabilities if not implemented securely. On screen, show a block diagram with arrows showing data flowing through multiple blocks, labeled 'Mode of Operation'. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Modes of Operation and Side Channels
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a block diagram with arrows showing data flowing through multiple blocks, labeled 'Mode of Operation'.

sources.excerpt: This course examines current topics in Systems. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Distributed Systems cluster, the Architecture and Operating Systems cluster, the Security cluster, or some combination of these three clusters. Contact Hours: Lecture 3

sources.excerpt: The Secure Software Development Framework groups practices into four practice groups. Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development. Protect the Software prevents unauthorized access to code and development artifacts. Produce Well-Secured Software addresses security requirements, design, verification, and release. Respond to Vulnerabilities identifies, analyzes, remediates, and learns from discovered weaknesses. Security requirements should be tracked throughout development. Verification provides evidence that selected practices and controls were performed. Security reasoning identifies assets, trust boundaries, threats, controls, evidence, residual risk, and responsibilities.
sources.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework

sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: Cryptographic standards define approved algorithms and parameters. Encryption supports confidentiality when keys and modes are used correctly. Message authentication and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity in different ways. Random number generation supports keys, nonces, and other security parameters. Key management covers generation, distribution, storage, use, rotation, revocation, and destruction. Modes of operation define how a primitive processes data larger than one block. Validation checks implementations against specified requirements. Security depends on the complete protocol and implementation, not only an algorithm name. Analysis also considers side channels and migration requirements.
